culture: Shoeshiners (boleros) work on the street and in plazas, giving shoes a shine from a raised chair
Customers are invited to climb up on the chair (subir a la silla)
Polish is called grasa; grasa café means brown polish
Shoeshine process: brush off dust, apply polish, brush, then buff with a cloth
Brillo fuerte (strong shine) versus brillo suave (soft shine) are options
Shoeshiners take pride in a good shine and in long years at their trade
A shoeshiner may shine about fifteen pairs a day
La Roma is a neighborhood (colonia) in Mexico City where people work and shoeshiners have customers
Shoeshiners have regular customers who come every week
Shoes are seen as telling about a person; well-cared-for shoes (bien cuidados) are valued
Black (el negro) shoes with a good shine are seen as elegant
Polite address terms: joven (young one) and usted, plus courteous phrases like con mucho gusto and pase, pase
A mirror shine (brillo de espejo) is a more advanced shine technique
Common farewell: ¡Hasta luego!
